rubrics.rubric: Are the required month-end close deliverables present with the specified workbook structure?
criterion: December_2024_Month_End_Close.xlsx contains exactly the five required sheets in the required order.
The five sheet names exactly match Reconciliation, Discrepancies, AP Reconciliation, Journal Entries, and Schedule C Summary.
December_2024_Variance_Memo.txt is present as a readable plain-text memo.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Reconciliation sheet provide a source-grounded two-sided bank reconciliation to one true cash balance?
criterion: The bank side starts from the December bank statement closing balance.
The bank side lists each supported outstanding check individually and applies it with the correct sign.
The bank side separately identifies any deposits in transit or bank errors supported by the named inputs.
The book side starts from the cash book ending balance and accounts for source-supported fees, interest, bank-only transactions, and book errors.
The adjusted bank balance and adjusted book balance equal the same stated true cash balance.
The sheet reports separate counts of bank-side and book-side reconciling items.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Discrepancies sheet completely and accurately document disagreements among the bank statement, cash book, vendor invoices, and AP aging?
criterion: The sheet uses the required discrepancy columns or clearly equivalent columns containing the same information.
Each material cross-source disagreement appears in its own row.
For a shared check number or reference, every differing field is identified rather than only the amount difference.
Each difference and proposed resolution is arithmetically correct and traceable to the named inputs.
Documented uncertainty is preserved when the supplied evidence does not establish a unique resolution.

rubrics.rubric: Does the AP Reconciliation sheet produce a complete vendor-level November-to-December rollforward?
criterion: Each vendor appearing in the opening AP aging, December invoices, or supported December payments is represented.
Each row computes opening balance plus December invoices minus December payments equals December 31 ending balance.
Invoice numbers and payment references are included where supplied.
Partial payments, unpaid December invoices, disputed balances, and uncertain payment applications remain visible in the ending balance or are explicitly resolved from source evidence.
The total ending AP agrees with the sum of the vendor rows.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Journal Entries sheet present all source-supported book corrections in valid double-entry form?
criterion: Each entry provides an entry identifier, date, debit account, credit account, amount, and memo.
Debits equal credits within every entry.
Account names are taken verbatim from chart_of_accounts_template.xlsx rather than replaced by Schedule C labels or unsupported aliases.
Source-supported cash book errors, omitted bank activity, fees, interest, and any adopted year-end AP treatment are addressed exactly once.
Items requiring owner or accountant judgment are identified without posting an unsupported final classification.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Schedule C Summary correctly map post-close figures to the official 2024 Schedule C and calculate budget variances?
criterion: The sheet uses the official 2024 Schedule C line numbers and category names.
Line 1 and every expense line with an actual or budgeted amount are included.
Corrected Actual values are traceable to the reconciled books and adopted adjusting entries rather than copied from raw cash book totals.
Budgeted Amount values agree with monthly_budget_dec2024.csv.
Variance dollars equal Corrected Actual minus Budgeted Amount.
Variance percentages use the same sign convention when the budget is nonzero and are documented as not applicable when the budget is zero.

rubrics.rubric: Does the variance memo give management a complete and internally consistent close summary?
criterion: The memo is addressed to Owner, Greenfield Landscaping Services LLC.
The stated true cash balance matches the Reconciliation sheet.
The memo states separate bank-side and book-side reconciling-item counts that match the workbook.
The memo summarizes the significant discrepancies and their source-grounded resolutions.
The memo identifies the largest corrected budget overruns.
The memo gives a documented recommendation for the disputed Acme Lawn Equipment invoice.
The memo lists the records or decisions the accountant still needs for year-end Schedule C reporting.
